title: Open a cocktail shaker after shaking: hold the tins, strike the seam where the small tin leans away, lift it off
instruction: The drink is shaken. Open the shaker: hold the big tin, strike the big tin's rim at the seam on the side where the small tin leans away, lift the small tin off, set both tins upright on the mat, let go of them and move your hands clear.
context: A tin-on-tin cocktail shaker (an 18 oz tin pushed into a 28 oz tin) seals itself on every shake: the cold drink draws the air inside down to a partial vacuum, and a straight pull does not part the tins. Difford's Guide: 'hold the larger can in one hand and break the seal between the two halves of the shaker' by 'tapping the base can with the palm of your other hand at the point where it meets the upper can'. A Bar Above: 'Hit your palm on the side of the shaker cups that has a little more space'. Bartenders (O*NET 35-3011.00; 756,390 US jobs, BLS OEWS May 2025) have the core task 'Mix ingredients, such as liquor, soda, water, sugar, and bitters, to prepare cocktails and other drinks.' (O*NET, USDOL/ETA, CC BY 4.0; O*NET is a trademark of USDOL/ETA). Every shaken drink ends with opening the shaker.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A black rubber bar mat, 30 x 42 x 1 cm, lies with its middle at (28, -4). On it stands a closed shaker with its axis at (28, 2): a weighted 28 oz tin (17.5 cm tall, 7.4 cm across its base, 9.2 cm across its mouth, 322 g, with 150 g of drink in it) and an 18 oz tin (15 cm tall, 8.1 cm across its mouth with a rolled rim, 150 g) pushed into it mouth-down, its mouth 14.6 cm above the big tin's base and leaning 2.5 degrees toward +y, so the gap at the seam is widest on the -y side. The arms start at their ready pose.
scoring: Read in the simulator from the tins' poses and the seal. 1.0: the seal broken by a blow at the big tin's rim (a fingertip of a hand not holding a tin, in the rim's top 1.5 cm or up to 2 mm above it, from 1 mm inside its wall to 1.2 cm outside, moving toward the tin's axis at 0.15 m/s or more relative to the tin, within 45 degrees of the side where the gap is widest, and touching the wall that step or the next), the small tin out, both tins upright within 10 degrees and standing on the mat (the small one either way up), every fingertip of both hands 5 cm clear of each tin's side or 5 cm above its top, held 1 s. 0.75: the seal broken, the small tin out, the big tin upright within 10 degrees and standing on the mat (its base within 1 cm of it) with every fingertip 5 cm clear of it. 0.5: the seal broken and the small tin out. 0.25: the seal broken by such a blow (every tier needs it). 0 at any time: a dent, the drink spilled, or a tin fallen off the table. The simulator has no dent or liquid, so it counts a blow of 1.0 m/s or more at the rim as a dent and the big tin tipped past 45 degrees once the seal is open as a spill (approximations). A real trial judges outcomes, with no blow-speed threshold and no spill tilt; the 10 degree limits still apply. It is filmed by a top camera, both wrist cameras and a side camera level with the seam. A blow is a hand not holding a tin striking the big tin's rim (its top 1.5 cm) within 45 degrees of the open side. The seal counts as broken by it only if the small tin comes out on the robot's first lift after that blow, turned no more than 10 degrees about its axis and tilted no more than 10 degrees from the big tin's axis before it comes free; a blow elsewhere, the holding hand squeezing the big tin at the seam, or a twist, rock or pry first scores 0. Before each trial the seal must hold a straight 20 N pull with a 10 degree twist each way (a luggage scale). For the 0.25 tier the judge lifts the small tin straight up with the big tin standing unheld: broken only if the big tin stays on the mat. A dent is a new one seen on the rim or wall under a raking light (photographed before and after), or either width of the mouth (along the open side's line and across it) changed by 0.5 mm or more (calipers, before sealing and after, the tins apart). A spill is 5 g or more of drink lost (the outsides wiped dry; both tins with their contents weighed against the sealed shaker before the trial, on a scale reading to 1 g; drink drained from the small tin onto the mat, soaked up and weighed, is not lost). Upright, on the mat, hands clear and the 1 s hold are read from the cameras.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at 240 Hz. No liquid: the drink is rigid mass in the big tin. The vacuum is two latches over the small tin's rim, locked until a blow opens them (a code coupling): a fingertip of a hand not holding a tin landing on the rim at 0.15 m/s or more, within 45 degrees of the open side. Sim-only approximations: that 0.15 m/s, a dent as 1.0 m/s, a spill as a tilt past 45 degrees (a real trial judges each by outcome), the 2.5 degree lean, 16-stave walls. Fingers stand in for the palm.
reset_notes: One fixed layout; no seed changes the scene. Before each real trial: about 150 ml of chilled water and ice in the big tin, the small tin seated with one firm press at its natural lean, shaken 10 s, the seal checked against a 20 N pull, the gap's wide side turned to -y.
